study.title: Psalm 80 Restore us, O God, and make your face shine
study.overview: This psalm is a Community lamentation. The people cry to God who led him as a shepherd, remembering his presence among the cherubim, his saving action in the past, and the image of the vineyard that he himself planted. Prayer insists three times on the request for restoration, showing that hope is not in national strength or on its own merits, but in the favorable presence of God. The text also exposes the pain of a humiliated people surrounded by enemies and apparently devastated, but still firm in asking the Lord to return to action.

outline.title: Clarment to the Shepherd of Israel
outline.explanation: The initial verses invoke God as the Shepherd of Israel and ask him to awaken his power to save. The repetition of "restaurants" and "make your face shine" reveals the total dependence on God's favorable presence, understood as the only hope of deliverance.

outline.title: The pain of a people under rebuke
outline.explanation: Here the psalmist asks how much God will be angry with the prayer of his people and describes collective humiliation: tears as food, drink of tears and mockery of neighbors. The request for restoration reappears, showing that distress is taken directly to God rather than being hidden.

outline.title: The transplanted and devastated vineyard, with final appeal for restoration
outline.explanation: The psalm recalls the history of the vineyard brought from Egypt, planted and made vast, but then broken and surrendered to destruction. The people ask God to return, visit the vineyard and protect the man from your right hand. The psalm ends as it began: with supplication so that God may make his face shine and grant salvation.

study.context: The notes indicate that this psalm may have arisen in the context of the fall and captivity of the northern tribes, or of another great affliction of Israel. There is a memory of the Exodus and the plantation of the nation as a vineyard of God. It is not necessary to accurately define a unique historical occasion to understand the scenario: the community is humiliated, weakened and asking for the Lord's intervention.
study.theology: The psalm teaches that the restoration of God is deeper than political relief: it involves the renewal of the relationship between the Lord and his people. The image of the pastor highlights care, direction and saving power; the image of the vineyard highlights election, planting, growth and also discipline when there is infidelity. The repetition of the request for God's face to shine suggests that true salvation depends on the Lord's reconciling presence. There is also an axis of covenant: the people appeal to God on the basis of what he has already done, not in his own dignity. In an evangelical Christian perspective, the notes allow us to see in the figure of the "man of your right hand" a possible reference to the chosen king of God, and also a reading that recalls the need for a restorative representative; this is an interpretation, not an unequivocal statement of the verse.

scholarViews.insight: The psalm may have originated in the remnant of the northern kingdom after its fall, and the request for restoration relies on the image of God as the Shepherd of Israel and as God of hosts.
The church is depicted as a vine planted by God, weak and dependent on sustenance, but also precious and fruitful; the metaphor serves to ask for mercy and grace.
The expression "does your face shine" is understood as the request for God to show reconciliation and favor, so that the people know that they are no longer under their displeasure.

questions: What changes when God's people learn to turn their shame into sincere prayer rather than silent despair?
How does the image of God as a Pastor correct our expectations when we seek security in human or national power?
In what ways does the repetition of "restaura" help to shape a persevering faith in times of discipline and loss?
study.practice: Take to God, in specific prayer, the situation in which you need restoration, without trying to disguise the pain. Remember, before him, the past acts of care and salvation, and ask not only external solution, but also the brightness of his face, that is, his favorable and reconciling presence. If your community lives discouragement or wear and tear, pray collectively with this psalm, asking God to visit his "vinha" and renew his faithfulness.
study.uncertainty: The musical title "Susanedute" and the exact historical occasion of the psalm are not safely identifiable only by the notes provided. The notes allow two interpretative possibilities for verse 17: reference to the kingdom of the north as chosen people, or to the king of the David dynasty; it is not possible to conclude with certainty which of them the text intends in the foreground. Nor can one say, from this material, a closed identification of all the symbolic details of the vineyard and the man of your right hand.
